meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'you', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Спасибо, спасибо! Как вы все знаете, я родился и вырос в Синеозерске.
examples.trans: Thank you, thank you! As you all know, I was born and grew up in Sineozersk.
And does the governor support you?

examples.text: Как вы все знаете, я родился и вырос в Синеозерске.
examples.trans: As you all know, I was born and grew up in Sineozersk.

meanings.note: Common feminine noun meaning 'pizza' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: If they're late, the pizza is free.
Let's order a pizza.

examples.text: Анатолий Иванович, тут доставка пиццы. Пишут, доставим за десять минут.
examples.trans: Anatoly Ivanovich, there's pizza delivery here. They write: we'll deliver in ten minutes.

meanings.note: Prefix 'за-' marks beginning an action, covering, or stopping by along the way (stem 'казывать'). Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to order', paired with 'заказать'.

examples.trans: Call and order pizza!
What will you order?

examples.text: Ладно, звони в свою пиццу. Заказывай!
examples.trans: All right, call your pizza place. Go ahead and order!

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian discourse particle adding conversational nuance meaning 'yes, indeed', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: Oh yeah?
Yes, it's me.
Oh yeah? When?

meanings.note: Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to hold'.

examples.trans: Here you go, this is for you.
Grab him!
All right, here you go. There, look.

meanings.note: Common feminine noun meaning 'thousand' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: That means thousands of jobs.
A thousand roubles.

examples.text: Мы построим кластер. Это тысячи рабочих мест.
examples.trans: We will build the cluster. That means thousands of jobs.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian spatial or relational preposition meaning 'for', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: We could open a salon for you.
This is for you.

examples.text: Для вас можно открыть салон красоты.
examples.trans: We could open a beauty salon for you.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'to you', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: Dad, did you bring any gum?
And this is for you. A toy car!

examples.text: У тебя же есть ещё. Дай хоть одну.
examples.trans: But you've still got some. Give me just one.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'nothing', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: There's nothing left.
I don't know anything.

examples.text: Ну что, очкарик? Видишь, ничего не осталось.
examples.trans: Well, four-eyes? See, there's nothing left.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian discourse particle adding conversational nuance meaning 'not', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: Chef, I didn't take it.
I don't know.
There wasn't enough money.

жалко.gloss: feel sorry for; it's a pity

meanings.en: feel sorry for; it's a pity
meanings.note: Manner/predicative adverb in '-о', derived from the neuter short form of the corresponding adjective.

examples.trans: I just feel sorry for him.

examples.text: Что за глупость? Эдик, мне его просто жалко.
examples.trans: What nonsense is that? Edik, I just feel sorry for him.
Edik, I just feel sorry for him.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian pronominal determiner meaning 'all, whole; everyone, everything', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: Everything's fine.
As you all know...
Share with everyone.

meanings.note: Prefix 'до-' marks reaching a boundary or finishing the remainder of an action (stem 'брый'). Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('kind; good').

examples.trans: Good evening!
She is very kind.

examples.text: Добрый вечер, Вика. С Новым годом!
examples.trans: Good evening, Vika. Happy New Year!

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian clause-linking conjunction meaning 'and, but; so', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: And this is for you.
And where's the toy car?
Dad, did you bring any gum?

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian conversational adverb meaning 'where', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: Where's my toy car?
Where's Dad?

examples.text: А где машинка? Где моя машинка?
examples.trans: Hey, where's the toy car? Where's my toy car?

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian discourse particle adding conversational nuance meaning 'so, then; like that', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: So I shouldn't wait for you?
That's good like that.
So I shouldn't wait for you tonight?

забрать.gloss: to take back, to take away

meanings.en: to take back, to take away
meanings.note: Prefix 'за-' marks beginning an action, covering, or stopping by along the way (stem 'брать'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to take back, to take away', paired with 'забирать'.

examples.trans: He will withdraw the statement.
I'll take the keys.

examples.text: Поговори с Аракеляном. Пусть он заберёт заявление.
examples.trans: Talk to Arakelyan. Get him to withdraw his statement.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian spatial or relational preposition meaning 'on, onto; for', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: The programme is on the website.
He is running for a second term.

examples.text: Я очень люблю наш город. Поэтому я иду на второй срок.
examples.trans: I love our town very much. That's why I'm running for a second term.

meanings.note: Common masculine noun meaning 'entrance' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: There at the cemetery is the main entrance.
Where is the entrance to the metro?
We will open this entrance right now.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'that', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Это хорошо, что готово. А то мы уже начали беспокоиться.
examples.trans: It's good that it's ready. We were starting to worry.

examples.text: А если я не скажу, то что? Ты мне ухо отрежешь?
examples.trans: And if I don't tell you, then what? Will you cut my ear off?

examples.text: А если я не скажу, то что?
examples.trans: And if I don't tell you, then what?

meanings.note: Common masculine noun meaning 'pretext, excuse' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: А то ты перлог, вот, достала уже.
examples.trans: That pearl barley of yours has driven me crazy already.

examples.text: Вам не предложат хорошо прожаренный стейк.
examples.trans: They will not offer you a well-done steak.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian discourse particle adding conversational nuance meaning 'here is; (emphasis) that's', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: All right, here you go. There, look.
There, look.
You'll see!

достать.gloss: to take out, to get, to reach

meanings.en: to take out, to get, to reach
meanings.note: Prefix 'до-' marks reaching a boundary or finishing the remainder of an action (stem 'стать'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to take out, to get, to reach', paired with 'доставать'.

examples.trans: And take his eye out with a spoon.
He took his phone out of his pocket.

examples.text: Вы понимаете, что вы нас достали уже?
examples.trans: Do you understand that you've made us sick of you already?

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian conversational adverb meaning 'already', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Я уже четыре года работаю мэром.
examples.trans: I've been mayor for four years now.
Dad is already home.
I'm already home.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'this, that; it is', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: That's mine.
And this is for you.
And this is for you. A toy car!

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian pronominal determiner meaning 'my, mine', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: Where's my toy car?
That's mine.
No. That's mine.

meanings.note: Common masculine noun meaning 'friend' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: This is Vanya, my childhood friend.

examples.text: Это Паша, мой заместитель. Это Ваня, друг моего детства.
examples.trans: This is Pasha, my deputy. This is Vanya, my childhood friend.

meanings.note: Prefix 'про-' indicates movement through, completion, or missing the mark (stem 'тивопоказанный'). Adjective formed with the common Slavic suffix '-н-' from a noun/verb root. Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('contraindicated, forbidden').

examples.trans: Pals, that is strictly forbidden for you.

examples.text: Сегодня у шефа очень противопоказанный день в ресторане.
examples.trans: Today the chef is having a very contraindicated day at the restaurant.

meanings.note: Prefix 'по-' forms perfective verbs or marks a brief/onset action (stem 'просить'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to ask (for), to request', paired with 'просить'.

examples.trans: I wanted to ask you something.
Ask Mum.
Arkash, I wanted to ask you something.

meanings.note: Common feminine noun meaning 'chicken' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: We're having chicken for dinner.
I don't want chicken.
There's chicken, over there.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian spatial or relational preposition meaning 'with', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: Share with everyone.
I'm with Dad.
Share it all equally with everyone, understand?

meanings.note: Common masculine noun meaning 'pineapple' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: Next you will be asking for chicken with pineapple?

examples.text: На нашей кухне уже есть новый ананас.
examples.trans: In our kitchen there is already a new pineapple.

meanings.note: Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('favourite, beloved').

examples.text: А ты готовишь мой любимый торт со сгущёнкой!
examples.trans: And you make my favourite condensed milk cake!
This is my favourite book.

examples.text: А ты готовишь мой любимый торт со сгущёнкой! До вечера, Марина.
examples.trans: And you make my favourite condensed milk cake! See you tonight, Marina.
